_comment: Unitree S288 BAM parameters, measured on one unit (ID 0) on 2026-09-11 at 12.0 V, case 55-60 C, free shaft. Output-side N.m throughout (the gearbox is 70070/243 = 288.354:1). FOC current loop => no kt/R needed. Everything under _robust was measured without fitting; _fit_* is the model fit. See bam_data/S288_BAM_汇总表.md (friction) and bam_data/S288_dynamics_测量记录.md (delay / compliance / backlash / inertia) for the runs behind each number.
motor: Unitree S288 (ID 0, firmware version not read)

_measurement.friction: velocity sweep, kp=0 kd=2, paired +/- to cancel gravity and offset, 9 speeds; plus a pure feedforward torque ramp for stiction
_measurement.command_delay: torque step +-0.02 N.m, both below the 0.0365 N.m breakaway so the shaft cannot move; 80 transitions fitted to td + first-order rise
_measurement.backlash: each of 3 positions reached from below and from above, 1.8 s settle, |v|=0 at measure time; hysteresis = gap(from below) - gap(from above)
_measurement.torque_source: the servo's own rotor torque feedback (256000 counts = 1 N.m); it tracked the commanded feedforward to within ~2-6% with a -3 count offset
_measurement.loop: 6.1-6.4 kHz blocking request/response over USB-CDC; one frame = 0.16 ms
caveats: armature is NOT measured. A free-body servo cannot yield it: the reaction torque equals the output torque (20-120 mN.m), which is at or above what the bench can hold and always above the 0.025 N.m needed to move at all, so the housing slips. Both a torque-step and a sine method returned ~5e-4 kg.m^2 — two orders of magnitude below the ~0.1 expected from a 1.2e-6 kg.m^2 rotor reflected through 288:1 — and the torque correlated with velocity (+0.67) but not acceleration (-0.03). Clamp the body and re-run bam_dynamics.py; that number is not a property of the servo.

backlash of 0.0184 rad (1.056 deg, repeatability 0.014 deg) is measured between the rotor-derived output angle and the output-side encoder. It contradicts the statement that the output encoder removes the need for a backlash model.

q_offset here is the measured constant offset between the two encoders of this unit (-1.63 deg, varying 0.4 deg with position, which includes the 13-bit output encoder's own non-linearity) — not an absolute joint zero.
no voltage sensitivity (only a 12 V supply) and no current-limit / peak torque measurement (no weights or stall rig). Temperature drift over 55-60 C was within +/-0.002 N.m.
